From Pointer Semantics to Categorical Structure

5 min read
1 hour ago

--

Four formal corrections close this out, all of them about typing Trace correctly — a fitting last step, since getting types right has been the through line of every revision in this series.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Separating Syntax, Structure, and ManifestationTrace must return a morphism, not a category
Writing Trace_t^{(n)} : P̂ ⇀ C_t was a type error of exactly the kind this series has been hunting down elsewhere: C_t is a category, not a set of routes an ordinary function can return an element of. What Trace actually needs to produce is a morphism of C_t, typed by its source and target:
Trace^{(n)}_t : P̂ ⇀ Mor(C_t)
Mor(C_t) = ⨿_{p,q ∈ P̂} Hom_{C_t}(p, q)or, written out concretely for a given input:
Trace^{(n)}_t(x) = c : p → q, c ∈ Hom_{C_t}(p, q), x ∈ ↓pThe dependent condition x ∈ ↓p matters, and it's the same subtlety Exec's earlier fix already surfaced: the input x is not generally the morphism's source object. In the running example from axiom A4, the traversed morphism is c : profile.cards.primary → wallet, but the input being resolved is x = profile.cards.primary.income — an extension of the source, x ∈ ↓p, not the source itself. Trace returns the typed morphism together with the guarantee that the actual input lives in its domain cone.
The pointer-free case needs its own object, not a bare identity
Trace^{(n)}_t(x) = id was informal in the same way — a category has no identity without an object to anchor it; every identity is id_p : p → p for some specific p. For a pointer-free resolution, the natural anchor is the path itself:
Trace^{(n)}_t(x) = id_x : x → xwhich composes correctly with everything already established: F_t(id_x) = id_{↓x}, so F_t(id_x)(x) = x, and therefore:
Exec_{t,γ}(id_x, x) = R_{t,γ}(x)— resolving a path with no pointer involved is exactly the special case where the structural layer contributes nothing and contextual resolution acts directly on the input. When a pointer is found — including one discovered at a prefix of x rather than at x itself — Trace instead returns c : p → q with x = p.s for some suffix s, and the same formula applies uniformly across both cases.
Two different partialities, not one
Saying R_{t,γ} was "where the only real partiality in the whole system lives" directly contradicted having just defined Trace^{(n)}_t as partial. The fix is to name two distinct kinds of partiality rather than pick one:
R_{t,γ} : P̂ ⇀ M — semantic partiality: a syntactically valid position may simply manifest nothing
Trace^{(n)}_t — operational partiality: a fuel-bounded evaluation may not complete a finite traceR_{t,γ} is where semantic partiality lives — a well-formed path can be entirely valid and still resolve to ⊥, for reasons unrelated to any pointer at all (nothing was ever written there, or the observer lacks the authority to see it). Trace_t^{(n)}may additionally be operationally partial, for a different reason entirely: because a bounded, finite evaluation procedure — src/core-index.ts: resolveIndexPointerPath's fuel-limited loop, or the unbounded-but-still-finite-stack outer recursion through self.readPath — need not complete before it must stop. These are not competing claims about where "the" partiality is; they're two separate sources of it, at two different layers.
ConeSubst(P̂) is a deliberately restricted category, not the category of all cone maps
Left unstated, “category of cone substitutions” invites a reader to imagine something much larger — every possible function between principal cones, which would generally be neither thin nor chaotic. That was never what was being defined. ConeSubst(P̂) is not the category of all cone maps; it is the deliberately restricted category containing exactly the canonical prefix-replacement map between each pair of principal cones — one specific morphism per ordered pair, π_{p,q}(p.s) = q.s, and nothing else. Its chaotic structure — every hom-set a singleton, every morphism invertible — is a direct consequence of that restriction, not an incidental property of "substitutions between cones" in general.
Faithfulness is a per-hom-set property, not a property of one walked route
F_t collapsing a single walked route "faithfully when no other route could have produced the same relocation" read as a claim about one execution, when faithfulness is inherently a statement about an entire hom-set. The precise version: on a hom-set Hom_{C_t}(p, q), F_t is injective exactly when that hom-set contains at most one route. Route information is preserved exactly for source–target pairs that admit at most one formal chain — and lost exactly for the pairs that admit more than one, regardless of which particular chain any single evaluation happened to walk.
The fully typed pipeline
H_t --fold_LWW--> G_t --FreeCat--> C_tFor a concrete evaluation of a path x:
Trace^{(n)}_t(x) = c : p → q, x ∈ ↓p (or id_x : x → x when no pointer is involved)F_t(c) : ↓p → ↓q
F_t(c)(x) ∈ ↓qRuntimeEval^{(n)}_{t,γ}(x) = R_{t,γ}( F_t(Trace^{(n)}_t(x))(x) ), when the trace is definedwith the pointer-free case collapsing cleanly to RuntimeEval^{(n)}_{t,γ}(x) = R_{t,γ}(x), and the axiom-A4 case instantiating as c : profile.cards.primary → wallet, x = profile.cards.primary.income, F_t(c)(x) = wallet.income, resolved through secret-branch decryption to 1000.
Verdict
Six typed stages, each carrying exactly what the next one needs and nothing it doesn’t:
history → active graph → available routes → typed traversed route → canonical relocation → contextual manifestationH_t records every declaration ever made. G_t folds that into what's currently active. C_t = FreeCat(G_t) holds every formally possible route those active edges permit — a space of possibilities, unconcerned with any particular execution. Trace_t^{(n)}(x) picks out one typed morphism of C_t — a genuine chain, or the identity at x when no pointer was needed — that a specific, fuel-bounded evaluation actually produced, and may itself be undefined when that evaluation fails to complete. F_t sends that morphism to its canonical net relocation in the deliberately restricted, chaotic category ConeSubst(P̂), faithfully wherever the corresponding hom-set of C_t had nowhere else to collapse from, and lossily wherever it did. R_{t,γ} takes the resulting path and decides, under a specific observer and mode, whether it manifests a value, a family, a history, or nothing — its own partiality, semantic rather than operational, answering a different question than Trace's ever did.

.me is not a category because pointers happen to compose. It is an event log, folded into an active graph, generating a free category of formally possible routes, from which a fuel-bounded evaluator extracts one typed, possibly-undefined trace per read, which a deliberately restricted structural functor reduces to a canonical relocation exactly as far as that route's hom-set permits, over which a separately, semantically partial contextual resolution finally decides what — if anything — the resulting position manifests.
